item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 20, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Apple Podcasts says video is delivering major audience gains for leading shows. In a new PodBiz interview, executive Jake Shapiro revealed that top podcasts adding video saw audiences grow more than 20 percent, while new followers jumped over 130 percent. Apple's HLS technology also creates new opportunities for advertising across audio and video.
Turning to industry honors,
The 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards take over Miami Thursday, October 22, with 16 musical performances airing live on Telemundo and Peacock. Wisin, Ivy Queen, Ozuna and Manuel Turizo are among the performers. The ceremony will also honor Rosalía, Rubén Blades, Cristian Castro and Fuerza Regida, while introducing its first-ever fan-voted award. The broadcast begins at 8 p.m. Eastern.
In television news,
Jon Stewart is staying with Comedy Central's The Daily Show through December 2028. Stewart will continue hosting Mondays and serving as executive producer, while the show's news team handles Tuesday through Thursday. The extension follows two Emmy wins and strong ratings growth, with The Daily Show generating 1.9 billion social media views this year.
Turning to radio,
Audacy has launched US 96.5, Philadelphia's newest country radio station, featuring artists like Morgan Wallen, Luke Combs and Jelly Roll. The station is commercial-free through October 24, with its weekday lineup beginning October 26. A new morning show will be announced soon. US 96.5 becomes Audacy's 24th country station nationwide.
In radio news,
Rob Wagman will lead Manna, SonicTrek Media’s new localized Contemporary Christian radio format. The service will pair market-specific music and content with radio personalities, including longtime host Sparkle. Wagman previously worked with KFSH in Los Angeles and WAY-FM.
Turning to television,
Fox Corporation is making changes to its legal leadership. Chief Legal and Policy Officer Adam Ciongoli will step down December first, transitioning to a special advisor role through June 2028. Nicholas Trutanich, currently Principal Deputy General Counsel, will become General Counsel, reporting directly to CEO Lachlan Murdoch. Trutanich joined FOX in 2021 and previously served as U.S. Attorney for Nevada. The company is also adjusting its government relations reporting structure.
In radio news,
Audacy is bringing The Bret Mega Show to Atlanta mornings on Star 94.1. Hosted by Bret Mega and Anna Bohlmann, the program airs weekdays from six to ten Eastern. The personality-driven show also airs in Kansas City, St. Louis and Wichita, expanding its reach across four Audacy markets.
Turning to television,
Telemundo Las Vegas has named Alejandro Sánchez a multimedia journalist for its local newscasts. Sánchez joins KBLR from Telemundo 40 in the Rio Grande Valley, where he covered immigration and border communities. His background also includes international reporting and production work for TelevisaUnivision. He began his new role Monday.
And finally,
The Academy of Country Music Awards will return to Las Vegas on May sixteenth, twenty twenty-seven, with tickets now on sale. The sixty-second annual ceremony will stream worldwide on Prime Video from the MGM Grand Garden Arena. Last year's event generated an estimated fifty-three million dollars for the Las Vegas economy, while attracting more than one hundred fifty-three million social media video views.
